about: TAU block parameters (tools/claims-v3/tau/README.md). A schedule entry is [sampler every_ms, kind, burst seconds(, sampler seconds)]; kind idle holds no burst. Each entry is one sampler window: timeout <timeout_s> ettelem sample --seconds <sampler seconds, default sampler_seconds> --every-ms <rate>, with the burst's host process launched pre_burst_s after the sampler's first line. A sampler that gives no line in first_line_max_s (or exits) is a failed start: retried up to sampler_attempts times, with one queue drain after drain_after_failed_starts failures (never on aifoundry1, whose stock dev_mngt_service opens card 0: there the block writes tau/STOP and ends after a1_stop_after_failed_starts failures in one window, or any SIGKILL). A first line so late that pre + setup_allow + burst + post_burst_min no longer fit in timeout_s is a late start: no burst, the window is repeated (at most burst_tries windows per entry). The full schedule's bursts are put in a seeded order per pass (shuffle_seed + pass; the leading idle window stays first). The block ends at stop_c (die mean) and does not start its bursts when the idle window's die mean is above start_max_c.

aifoundry2.role: third card (only after DV2 ends: TAU_A2_OK=1)
